messages:
maria.chen: Heads-up — we need to reconcile audit event TTL + redaction policy after the RBAC change that landed this morning. Customer-facing events (billing, auth) currently include some metadata that could be PII. Need alignment on schema flags and KMS behavior. cc @akash.patel @jordan.lewis

sec-bot: New policy applied: `audit-retention-default-90d` to workspace `internal` (see https://intra.redwood/policies/audit-retention). :lock:

akash.patel: Quick notes: 1) Forensics customers will want >=90d raw logs; 2) Compliance teams want sensitive chunks redacted ASAP. We should avoid making a breaking rename — add optional fields instead. :thinking_face:

akash.patel: Proposal: add two optional fields on audit events: `sensitivity` ("low|medium|high") and `retention_tier` ("hot|warm|cold"). Add `redact_level` ("none|partial|full") for consumer-facing delivery. Also add `kms_wrapped: true|false` + `kms_key_id` when applicable.

maria.chen: example snippet of how an event could look ingest-side (pseudo):
```json
{"actor":"svc-ingest","action":"user.login","sensitivity":"medium","retention_tier":"hot","redact_level":"partial","kms_wrapped":true,"kms_key_id":"projects/prod/keys/audit-1"}
```

jordan.lewis: Important: any new fields must be optional and documented in the event catalog. SIEM customers read the raw `message` field, so we need to prevent silent regressions. Migration plan: 1) Add fields, 2) update router to populate defaults, 3) 30d dual-write where old consumers can opt-in to new fields, 4) deprecation notice.

clare_ng: From product: customer-facing names matter. We should map `redact_level` -> `customer_visibility` in the docs for external audit exports. Also need a clear table of examples (billing event with partial redaction vs. admin change full redaction).

akash.patel: KMS implications: if `kms_wrapped=true`, we can store encrypted PII and allow reversible disclosure for forensics (with proper RBAC + KMS ACL). If `kms_wrapped=false` and `redact_level=full`, we must permanently strip the field before storage. Need guidance from infra on key rotation semantics and access logs.

maria.chen: Open questions: - default `sensitivity` mapping (what makes an event high?) - who can request reversible unredaction (roles) - retention enforcement: will TTL be applied at object level or partition level?

jordan.lewis: I'll check with eng-infra about per-object TTL support on our storage (S3 lifecycle vs. DB TTL). If not supported, we fallback to partition-level retention and mark events with `retention_tier` for downstream compaction jobs.

akash.patel: Action items: I can draft the spec for the schema additions + KMS integration. Needs review from @clare_ng, @jordan.lewis, and legal/compliance. Will include sample consumer migration notes and a SIEM compatibility section.

clare_ng: Please include customer communication templates and a recommended mapping table for external exports. Also a short FAQ covering: "What happens to my existing audit exports?"

maria.chen: Decision (tentative): add optional `sensitivity`, `retention_tier`, `redact_level`, `kms_wrapped`, and `kms_key_id` fields. Implement dual-write + 30d opt-in for major consumers, then deprecate old blind format. Akash to own spec; Jordan to validate infra constraints; Clare to draft external messaging. :thumbsup:

akash.patel: I'll start a PR in `infra/audit-specs` and tag reviewers. ETA for draft: EOD Friday.

sec-bot: Reminder: Please file an RFC in `governance/rfcs` for persistent schema changes (template: https://intra.redwood/rfcs).

maria.chen: Thanks everyone — ping here when PR exists. If infra says per-object TTL is impossible, we may need to add `retention_effective_date` to support compaction jobs.

jordan.lewis: noted. Will report back by tomorrow EOD.

clare_ng: Thanks — will prep customer comms draft once spec lands.

maria.chen: closing thread for now, will reopen if blockers appear. :white_check_mark:
